title: Support-coefficient calculus for #257: divisor incidence, dilation, sunflowers and the squarefree barrier

concepts.label: Support divisor incidence
concepts.description: sc_A(n) = #{d in A : d divides n}, the coefficient of the binary Lambert rearrangement of the sum of 1/(2^a - 1) over A.

concepts.label: Boolean Mobius inversion
concepts.description: The Dirichlet identity sc_A = 1_A * zeta and its inverse mu * sc_A = 1_A, which makes the support recoverable from the coefficient.

concepts.label: Tempered binary carry orbit
concepts.description: An integer sequence U with U(N+1) = 2U(N) - q sc_A(N+1) and U(N)/2^N tending to zero; it exists exactly when the series has denominator q.

concepts.label: Dilation-difference pullback
concepts.description: The forward difference f(pn) - f(n) of a divisor-incidence coefficient, identified with the incidence of the pulled-back support {a : pa in A}.

concepts.label: Exact prime-power valuation layer
concepts.description: The set {d coprime to p : p^e d in A}, extracted by the difference of incidences at p^e n and p^(e-1) n.

concepts.label: Composite dilation defect
concepts.description: The support divisors of a*x other than a itself that do not already divide x, the exact error term when the dilating element is not prime.

concepts.label: Orthogonal petal bouquet
concepts.description: A sunflower-shaped support: a fixed frame Q absorbing all cores, plus pairwise-coprime petals of summable reciprocal mass.

concepts.label: Bounded-Omega support
concepts.description: A support whose members all have at most K prime factors counted with multiplicity.

concepts.label: Doubling residues and wrap digits
concepts.description: Least residues of p*2^n modulo an odd v, with the carry bit recording each wrap past v.

concepts.label: Reciprocal mass
concepts.description: The sum of 1/a over a in A, the Cesaro limit of the binary support-coefficient tails.

concepts.label: Dyadic prefix compression
concepts.description: Subtracting a reduced finite Mersenne prefix from a dyadic displayed value while keeping the odd part of the denominator uncancelled.

concepts.label: Greedy Mersenne orbit for one half
concepts.description: The greedy selection of Mersenne weights 1/(2^n - 1) against the target 1/2, with taken ranks, skipped ranks and dyadic safety.

concepts.label: Squarefree support incidence
concepts.description: The coefficient of the support of squarefree integers at least two, equal to 2^omega(n) - 1.

concepts.label: Block-certificate irrationality engines
concepts.description: The CertificateKernel engines that consume a first-block condition plus a middle-window budget. THREE of them accept an arbitrary support, not two: irrational_erdosSupportSeries_of_weighted_coeff_certificates (digitwise, b^r divides sc_A(N+r)); irrational_erdosSupportSeries_of_weighted_coeff_carry_certificates (carried aggregate, b^K divides the weighted first block); and irrational_coeff_series_of_weighted_coeff_low_carry_block_certificates (low-carry residue band, NO divisibility condition at all - only q * (V * b^(L-K) + C + (N+L+2)) < b^L for V = carrySum mod b^K), which applies to any support through erdosSupportSeries_eq_tsum_supportCoeff plus supportCoeff_le_self exactly as the other two do, even though no erdosSupportSeries-level wrapper has been written for it. The squarefree barrier closes the first two only.

concepts.label: Primitive prefix/residual shell split
concepts.description: The decomposition A = (A cap Iic X) union (A minus Iic X) and the first dyadic shell X < n <= 2X where the divisor shadow collapses to the membership bit.

concepts.label: Mobius-sign support
concepts.description: The Boolean supports {d : mu(d) = -1} and {d >= 2 : mu(d) = 1} obtained by discarding signs from the identity sum mu(d)/(2^d - 1) = 1/2.

concepts.label: Reduced modulus on a progression
concepts.description: Divisibility by a along My + c occupies one class modulo a/gcd(a,M), the correct replacement for a false coprimality assumption.

concepts.label: Mersenne achievement set
concepts.description: The set of reals of the form sum over A of 1/(2^a - 1) with 0 not in A; membership of the rational 1/2 would exhibit an Erdos #257 counterexample.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For any support A the divisor-incidence coefficient equals the Dirichlet convolution of the normalised support indicator with zeta, and the Mobius transform inverts it: mu * sc_A is the indicator of A on positive integers, and equals A exactly as a set once 0 is excluded from A.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Mobius inversion of an indicator function; classical (Mobius 1832, Dirichlet). The only new content is the zero-normalisation guard, which the file itself flags as necessary.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: An integer-valued arithmetic function is the divisor-incidence coefficient of some support if and only if its Mobius transform takes only the values 0 and 1 on positive integers; the support is then recovered as the set where that transform equals 1.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Immediate from invertibility of Dirichlet convolution by zeta; no search or finiteness input.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The number of divisors of n is at most twice the integer square root of n; consequently every support incidence coefficient is at most 2*sqrt(n) and the scaled binary tail of the incidence sequence is at most 2*sqrt(N) + 4.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The divisor-pairing bound tau(n) <= 2*floor(sqrt n) is textbook; Mathlib only carried the coarser tau(n) <= n, so the Lean statement is a formalisation gap fill, not a new theorem.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The value of the sum of 1/(2^a - 1) over A is rational if and only if the incidence sequence admits a tempered integer carry orbit; for a displayed fraction p/q the orbit is unique with multiplier q and initial value p.
open_antecedents: neither side is decided: for infinite A, that the left side fails is exactly Erdos #257, and no theorem in the corpus excludes a tempered carry orbit for an arbitrary infinite support
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Standard base-b carry/orbit reformulation of rationality; both sides are open, so this is a change of coordinates on the open problem rather than progress on it.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A support sums to exactly 1/2 if and only if its canonical affine denominator-two carry orbit is tempered; the scaled residual 2^N (1/2 - value) equals that carry halved minus the incidence tail, and for a finite prefix through N+1 the residual is (integer affine carry minus finite tail) over 2^(N+1).
open_antecedents: whether any support has value exactly 1/2 is open; both sides of this equivalence are undecided in the corpus

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Normalised nonempty supports with value p/q correspond, at the level of existence, to quotient-only Boolean Mobius carry certificates: positive integer orbits inside the square-root strip whose successive differences are divisible by q and whose carry quotient has Boolean Mobius transform. The support is reconstructed from the certificate rather than assumed.
open_antecedents: existence of a Boolean Mobius carry certificate for a given p/q is not decided anywhere in the corpus; for infinite supports its non-existence is exactly Erdos #257
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The file itself states no novelty claim. The equivalence eliminates the support variable but not the difficulty.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The support {2,3} has value 10/21 and its denominator-21 carry orbit is exactly the purely period-six cycle 10,20,19,17,13,26; the orbit is tempered, its differences are divisible by 21, its carry quotient recovers the incidence coefficient, and the Mobius transform of that quotient recovers the set {2,3}.

For a prime p and n coprime to p, the incidence of A at pn equals its incidence at n plus the incidence at n of the pullback {a : pa in A}; iterating along a pairwise-coprime list of primes gives the incidence of the product pullback at arguments coprime to the product.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: An exact elementary divisor split; almost certainly folklore, and the file explicitly disclaims any distributional or #257 consequence.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If every element of A has at most K prime factors counted with multiplicity, then pulling A back by any list of more than K primes gives identically zero incidence, so the corresponding iterated dilation difference vanishes at every argument coprime to the product.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Counting Omega of a product of primes; the annihilation is immediate once the pullback identity is available.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Kernel-checked instances of the dilation calculus: one difference on {2,3} extracts the multiples of 2, and two coprime prime differences annihilate {2,3} because its elements have Omega = 1.

In a finite-core orthogonal petal bouquet the rays are pairwise distinct and disjoint from the exceptional frame, the support is infinite, a foreign ray dividing a dilated argument forces its own petal to divide the undilated argument, and after any finite frame enlargement the gcd of an unselected ray with the frame is exactly its core, so its reduced modulus stays its full petal. A uniform petal rank ceiling R gives support Omega at most Omega(Q) + R.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary coprimality bookkeeping over an authored structure; the structure itself is a definition, not a theorem, so novelty here is definitional.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: There is an explicit infinite orthogonal petal bouquet with two genuinely different fixed cores: frame Q = 6, cores alternating between 2 and 3, petals the squares of the primes from the third onwards. Every member has exactly three prime factors with multiplicity, so the interface is non-vacuous on a bounded-Omega support.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A non-vacuity witness for an authored structure. It says nothing about the irrationality of the value of that support.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A uniform real bound of 16 on the binary incidence tail after a divisibility-certified slot pays every finite middle-window budget, and a forced-slot carry selector composes unconditionally into the carry-aware certificate supply once the support has one positive member. For an orthogonal petal bouquet the positivity clause is automatic.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Pure carry arithmetic. It moves the obligation, it does not discharge it.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If a support satisfies the forced-slot tail selector - for every K > 0 there is an N with 2^K dividing the carried first block and binary incidence tail at N+K at most 16 - then the sum of 1/(2^a - 1) over that support is irrational. In particular this holds for any orthogonal petal bouquet satisfying the selector.
open_antecedents: hselection : SunflowerForcedSlotTailSelection A, i.e. for all K > 0 there exists N with 2^K dividing the sum over r in Icc 1 K of supportCoeff A (N+r) * 2^(K-r), and binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) (N+K) <= 16. No declaration in the corpus proves this for any infinite support, and the file names it as the remaining analytic obligation.
hsupply : SunflowerForcedCarrySupply A, the same obligation in its carry-supply form
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The conclusion is unproved for every infinite support; the theorem is the socket, not the supply.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Divisibility by a along the progression My + c occupies at most one residue class modulo the reduced modulus a/gcd(a,M), giving at most Y/(a/gcd(a,M)) + 1 hits in a window of length Y; and if the frame divides one distinguished slot, any later hit is spaced from it by at least gcd(a,M).
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The reduced-modulus count for a linear congruence is elementary and classical; its value here is that it replaces a false coprimality assumption used earlier in the route.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For p prime, e >= 1 and n coprime to p, the incidence of A at p^e n minus its incidence at p^(e-1) n is exactly the incidence at n of the exact-valuation pullback {d coprime to p : p^e d in A}.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary layer count over the divisors of p^e n; it repairs the repeated-prime gap that the distinct-prime dilation identity leaves open.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Prime-power layer operators commute as integer finite differences, and the composite of two layers at distinct primes extracts the iterated exact-valuation pullback at arguments coprime to the product of those primes.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A two-fold iteration of the single prime-power layer identity; the module itself states it supplies no transport and no bounded-Omega endpoint.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Kernel-checked instances of the valuation layer: the third 2-adic layer of the singleton {8} contributes one new divisor at residual argument 1, and the mixed 2^2/3 layer of {12} contributes exactly one.

For a in A and x positive, the incidence of A at a*x equals its incidence at x, plus one when a does not already divide x, plus the composite dilation defect - the number of members of A dividing a*x that neither divide x nor equal a. On a support consisting only of primes the defect vanishes, recovering the prime-dilation formula.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: An exact finite counting identity; the file explicitly disclaims any correlation estimate or bounded-Omega irrationality consequence.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: In an orthogonal petal bouquet every composite dilation defect at a ray is either an exceptional finite-frame element or comes from a unique foreign ray whose petal already divides the undilated argument; hence the defect is at most the exceptional cardinality plus the incidence of the petal range at that argument.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Pointwise injection argument; the docstring notes it makes no appeal to lower-rank irrationality.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The smallest composite-defect witness: dilating by 6 on the support {2,6} creates both the distinguished member 6 and the lower-rank divisor 2, so the defect is exactly 1 and the exact identity records the extra term.

The incidence of A splits exactly into the incidences of its prefix through X and of its residual above X; on the first dyadic shell X < n <= 2X the residual incidence equals the plain membership bit, because a divisor of n exceeding X must be n itself. Subtracting the prefix carry scaled by q from the full carry scaled by D leaves exactly qD times the residual tail, whose forcing digit on that shell is therefore the membership bit.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary, but it is the exact place where the divisor shadow and the primitive bit coincide, which the route needs.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If a positive residual is at least 1/(qD) while its first dyadic shell and geometric far tail contribute at most K/2^X + 2/2^(2X), then 2^X <= qD(K+1); the same elementary pressure gives 2^m <= 4qD from a bound of 4/2^m. When the residual is a positive difference of two rationals the lower bound is supplied by the product of the actual reduced denominators.
open_antecedents: hupper : beta <= (K : R) / 2 ^ X + 2 / 2 ^ (2 * X) - a denominator-uniform analytic shell-plus-far-tail upper bound on the actual residual. The module docstring itself records that deriving denominator-uniform pressure from the analytic estimates remains the new global bottleneck; nothing in the corpus supplies this hypothesis.
hupper : beta <= 4 / 2 ^ m in the next-support variant
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The inequality itself is division-free elementary algebra; all mathematical weight sits in the unproved analytic hypothesis, and the corpus explicitly does not claim positive density or a Wang-Grau Ribas specialisation.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A positive difference of two rationals is at least the reciprocal of the product of their reduced denominators.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The elementary rational separation bound; the only added step over the corpus's own absolute-value form is removing the absolute value under strict positivity.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Splitting the signed identity sum over d of mu(d)/(2^d - 1) = 1/2 by sign gives that the Boolean support {d : mu(d) = -1} sums to 1/2 plus the entire positive-Mobius tail from d = 2 onwards; that tail contains the term 1/63 at d = 6, so the negative-Mobius support sums to strictly more than 1/2, in fact at least 1/2 + 1/63.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Rests on the classical signed Lambert identity sum mu(d)/(2^d - 1) = 1/2, which lives outside this zone (MersenneLambertLadder). The quantitative overshoot 1/63 is the corpus's own packaging.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Rules out exactly one route: taking the negative-Mobius indices as a Boolean support in the hope of realising 1/2. It does not decide whether some other infinite Boolean support sums to 1/2, it does not touch the greedy Mersenne route, it says nothing about the irrationality of the negative-Mobius value itself, and it is specific to base 2 and to the target 1/2.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The least residue of p*2^n modulo v satisfies the exact carry identity 2 r(n) = v w(n) + r(n+1) with wrap digit w(n) in {0,1}, is periodic along any doubling period, and shifts by absorbing 2^N into the starting numerator.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The binary long-division coordinates of a fraction with odd denominator.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Over one closed doubling cycle the least positive residues sum to the odd modulus times the number of wraps; equivalently, the sum of residues of p*2^j over a full period is v times the wrap count.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The classical repetend/digit-sum identity for the binary expansion of a fraction with odd denominator.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A closed doubling cycle of length h with numerator coprime to the modulus and exactly one wrap forces the modulus to be the Mersenne number 2^h - 1 and the starting residue to be a power of two below h. The same classification holds for the actual multiplicative order of 2.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary and very likely folklore for binary repetends; the corpus's contribution is that it replaces an earlier 446-orbit finite check by an algebraic argument.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For odd v > 1 the multiplicative order of 2 modulo v exists, is positive, is a doubling period, and the wrap count over one full order is positive.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Euler/Lagrange; standard group theory of (Z/v)^*.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Given an odd-denominator tail state for a support - an integer sequence u with u(n) = v times the binary incidence tail and u(n) congruent to p*2^n modulo v - the tail splits exactly as residue/v plus a nonnegative integer excess, the excess obeys sc_A(N+1) + excess(N+1) = wrap digit + 2 excess(N), and summing over one doubling period gives wrap count plus the summed excess.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A coordinate decomposition; it has content only once a tail state exists, which requires the rational-value hypothesis.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If the value of the support series equals p/(2^c v) with v positive, then the scaled tails from level c onwards form a positive integer state congruent to p*2^n modulo v, with numerator p positive; hence every consequence of the odd tail state applies under a rational-value assumption.
open_antecedents: hvalue : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (p : R) / ((2 ^ c * v : N) : R) - i.e. the support series takes a rational value. For infinite A this is precisely what Erdos #257 asserts is impossible, and nothing in the corpus proves or refutes it.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This is the entry point that makes the whole T9/T10/T13 layer conditional on the open rationality hypothesis.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If the reciprocal sum over A converges, the Cesaro mean of the binary incidence tails converges to that reciprocal mass, as does the mean of the partial sums of the incidence coefficients; the same holds after any finite shift.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The mean value of a divisor-incidence count is the classical Dirichlet density computation; the passage to binary tails is a Cesaro equivalence using the square-root envelope.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Given an odd tail state with doubling period h, the reciprocal mass of the support equals the wrap ratio (wrap count over h) plus the Cesaro mean of the tail excess; since the excess is nonnegative, the wrap ratio is a lower bound for the reciprocal mass, or the reciprocal sum diverges. In particular 1/h is such a lower bound whenever the wrap count is at least one.
open_antecedents: hstate : IsOddSupportTailState A p v u - existence of an odd-denominator tail state, which by the node rational_value_constructs_odd_tail_state is available only under the open assumption that the support series is rational
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: T9. An exact excess-mean identity; its force depends entirely on assuming a rational value.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If the support series equals p/(2^c v) with v odd and greater than one, then either the reciprocal sum over A diverges or it is at least the wrap ratio of p modulo v over the multiplicative order of 2 modulo v; when the numerator is coprime to v this gives the lower bound 1 over that order.
open_antecedents: hvalue : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (p : R) / ((2 ^ c * v : N) : R) - the open rationality hypothesis of Erdos #257 for infinite A
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A genuine necessary condition on any hypothetical rational support value, but it constrains rather than refutes: nothing here shows the constraint is unsatisfiable.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If F is a finite subset of A whose members all divide n, then the incidence at n is at least the cardinality of F, and the odd tail excess just before n is at least the collision surplus ceil((|F| - 1)/2). The bound holds in both the unshifted and the shifted normalisation.
open_antecedents: hstate : IsOddSupportTailState A p v u (or its shifted form) - available only under the open rationality hypothesis
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: T10. The pure counting part (card F <= supportCoeff A n) is unconditional; the surplus bound is not.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: At a common multiple L of a finite subset F of A the periodic excess spike improves the wrap-ratio bound: the reciprocal mass is at least the wrap ratio plus the collision surplus of F divided by L, or the reciprocal sum diverges.
open_antecedents: hstate : IsOddSupportTailState A p v u (or IsShiftedOddSupportTailState) - available only under the open rationality hypothesis

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If an infinite support has a dyadic rational value p/2^c, then either its reciprocal sum diverges or that sum exceeds 1; the mechanism is that any two distinct positive members force the excess to be at least 2 on a periodic set of positions.
open_antecedents: hvalue : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (p : R) / ((2 ^ c : N) : R) - the open hypothesis that an infinite support has a dyadic rational value
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A sharp-looking necessary condition on a dyadic counterexample, including the value 1/2. It does not exclude such a counterexample, since supports with reciprocal mass above 1 are abundant.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For an infinite support with a rational value p/(2^c v), the tail state is unbounded: at any common multiple L of a finite subset F of A the state satisfies 1 + v|F| <= 2 u(L - c - 1), and since F may be taken arbitrarily large the state exceeds every bound.
open_antecedents: hvalue : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (p : R) / ((2 ^ c * v : N) : R) - the open rationality hypothesis for an infinite support
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: T13. Unboundedness of the state is not by itself a contradiction, because the temperedness requirement is only u(n)/2^n tending to zero.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Exact computable validation of the wrap calculus on twelve modulus/order rows covering 446 coprime starting residues: every start has positive wrap count, the one-wrap condition holds exactly when the modulus is Mersenne and the start is a power of two, and the recorded minimum wrap counts for moduli 3, 5, 7, 15, 31 are attained.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Validation evidence only; the file states it is not the source of the universal classification.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Subtracting a fraction r/D with D odd from a dyadic rational p/2^c leaves a numerator coprime to D, so the reduced denominator of the residual is divisible by D and divides 2^c D: the odd part of the prefix denominator cannot cancel.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary coprimality of 2^c with an odd modulus; the useful part is that it is stated for the actual reduced denominator rather than a displayed one.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Every greedy decision for the target 1/2 against the Mersenne weights - take, skip, dyadic safety, two-channel cap violation, membership in the Mersenne/dyadic sliver - is equivalent to an explicit sign or window condition on a single integer excess numerator obeying E(n+1) = 2E(n) + L, with no real analysis left in the criterion.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A change of coordinates on the greedy algorithm; it decides nothing about whether the greedy run terminates or recurs.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The block take, dyadic safety and first-take-after predicates are invariant under multiplying numerator and denominator by a common positive factor, so they may be evaluated in raw uncancelled coordinates; all skips between a take and the next take are safe exactly when the block is adjacent or the last margin inequality holds.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Scale invariance is exactly what lets the argument avoid computing the gcd; no arithmetic content beyond that.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For a first take after a gap, the predecessor safety margin holds if and only if the reciprocal floor floor(2D/p) is not the Mersenne number 2^(b-1) - 1; the same criterion holds in raw and in reduced taken-block coordinates.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: An exact reformulation of the safety obstruction as a Mersenne coincidence of a floor; it does not show the coincidence can be excluded.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Safe bracketing together with nondecrease of the displayed numerator is not an inductive invariant of the greedy orbit: the state 7/(2*17) takes rank 3, producing 15/(2*119) with numerator increased, yet rank 4 is an unsafe skip with exact excess 1. The same failure survives lcm saturation over the Mersenne numbers through 127.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Refutes only the specific proposed induction (safe bracket plus numerator monotonicity), at specific states. It does not rule out a stronger inductive invariant, does not rule out the raw block margin or gcd overshoot supplies, and says nothing about whether the greedy run for 1/2 actually reaches these states.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Raw dyadic safety does not imply the gcd-scaled predecessor overshoot: the state 7/15 at rank 2 is safe and satisfies the raw overshoot bound while failing the gcd-scaled one, and an explicit factor-eleven state 39/539 shows the same at rank 5 with first take at rank 9.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Shows only that the gcd-scaled overshoot supply is strictly stronger than raw safety at particular states, so a proof of raw safety cannot be routed through the gcd-scaled criterion. It does not refute either supply, and it does not show these states occur on the actual greedy orbit for 1/2.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The Mersenne mass through twice the current depth is already below the current dyadic cap, and through 2m+2 further ranks below the two-channel cap; hence a dyadically unsafe skip forces every one of the next n+2 ranks to be taken, and a cap-violating skip forces the next 2n+4 ranks to be taken.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Geometric tail estimates on the Mersenne weights; unconditional and about the actual greedy orbit.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The forced-take block extracted from a cap violation cannot be extended by one more rank: the two-channel cap is strictly below the Mersenne prefix mass through 2m+3 ranks, and there is a real residual violating the cap whose remainder after the 2m+2 forced takes is already below the next weight.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Only shows that this particular tail-mass comparison cannot force a longer block. Longer forced blocks may still follow from a different estimate or from the actual greedy state; the sharpness witness is a relaxed real residual, not a residual known to occur on the greedy orbit for 1/2.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The analytic greedy take test at rank n+1 is exactly the arithmetic BlockTakeAt predicate on the actual displayed numerator and prefix denominator, and block dyadic safety at a skipped rank forces the greedy remainder below the next dyadic cap. Both statements are unconditional identities between an analytic and an arithmetic test; neither asserts anything about the value 1/2.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This is the hinge that turns the analytic greedy question into pure integer arithmetic. The half-membership consequence that used to sit in this node was split out during adversarial review into half_membership_from_actual_block_safety, because it carries an unproved supply hypothesis and this node did not name it.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If at every rank the actual greedy run for 1/2 skips, the displayed state is block dyadically safe at the next rank, then 1/2 lies in the Mersenne achievement set - that is, some support of exponents has sum of 1/(2^a - 1) equal to exactly 1/2, which for an infinite support would be a counterexample to Erdos #257. This is the base supply socket that every other half-membership node in this zone factors through.
open_antecedents: hsafe : for all n, if the actual greedy run skips rank n+1 (that is, mersenneWeight (n+1) is not at most greedyMersenneRemainder (1/2) n) then BlockDyadicSafeAt (halfGreedyResidualDisplayedNumerator n).natAbs (halfGreedyPrefixDenominator n) (n+1). The hypothesis is written inline rather than as a named predicate, which is why it escaped the ledger; no declaration in the corpus proves it, no finite computation can, and safe_bracket_plus_numerator_monotone_is_not_inductive refutes the obvious induction that would have produced it.
statement_nodes.engine: actual-state block dyadic safety (base socket for the raw-margin and gcd-overshoot supplies)
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Split out of greedy_take_predicate_equals_block_take_predicate during adversarial review. Nine of the ten half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_* theorems in DyadicPrefixCompression were already owned by conditional_implication nodes with a named open antecedent; this one was not, and it is the theorem the other lanes actually apply (lines 3219, 3240 and 3424 of the module).

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If at every skipped rank the integer excess satisfies 3 * 2^(n+1) * E(n) <= D(n), then 1/2 lies in the Mersenne achievement set, that is, some support of exponents has sum of 1/(2^a - 1) equal to exactly 1/2.
open_antecedents: hbound : HalfGreedySkippedExcessBound, i.e. for every n, if the greedy run skips rank n+1 then 3 * ((2 ^ (n+1)) * halfGreedyNextDyadicExcessNumerator n) <= halfGreedyPrefixDenominator n. No declaration in the corpus proves this, and no finite computation can establish it.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The conclusion 1/2 in the achievement set would exhibit a rational value for an infinite exponent support, i.e. a counterexample to Erdos #257; the antecedent is therefore expected to be hard or false, and nothing here decides which.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The skipped-rank excess bound need only be assumed on skips followed by a full forced take run: requiring it after a run of 2n+4 takes is already sufficient, and is in fact equivalent to the unrestricted bound; the weaker n+2 take-run form is also sufficient.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If every skipped rank of the greedy run for 1/2 is bracketed by consecutive actual takes whose source-coordinate raw margin inequality holds, then that skip is block-dyadically safe, and 1/2 lies in the Mersenne achievement set. It suffices to supply the witness only at skips that are not already safe.

hsupply : HalfGreedySkippedRawBlockMarginSupply and hsupply : HalfGreedyUnsafeSkipActualRawMarginSupply - the same obligation in raw-block and minimal unsafe-skip form; unproved
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A second, arithmetically different lane to the same conclusion as half_membership_from_skipped_excess_bound; the two are not known to be equivalent.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Block dyadic safety at rank k is exactly the unscaled predecessor overshoot inequality p <= 2D - p(2^k - 1); the gcd of D with 2^k - 1 always divides that overshoot, the gcd-scaled form is equivalent to a primitive-quotient comparison, and the gcd-scaled form implies safety.

If at every putatively unsafe skipped rank the gcd of the prefix denominator with 2^(n+1) - 1, times the displayed numerator, is at most the predecessor overshoot, then no unsafe skip exists and 1/2 lies in the Mersenne achievement set. The gcd-scaled and primitive-quotient forms of this supply are exactly equivalent, and an eleven-fold strengthening also suffices.
open_antecedents: hsupply : HalfGreedyUnsafeSkipGcdOvershootSupply - at every skipped and not-already-safe rank n, gcd(D(n), 2^(n+1) - 1) * |num(n)| <= 2 D(n) - |num(n)| (2^(n+1) - 1); unproved
hsupply : HalfGreedyUnsafeSkipPrimitiveOvershootSupply - the equivalent primitive-quotient form; unproved
hsupply : HalfGreedyUnsafeSkipElevenGcdOvershootSupply - the eleven-fold strengthening; unproved
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A third distinct lane to 1/2 in the achievement set. The zone contains a finite state where raw safety holds but the gcd-scaled bound fails, so this lane is genuinely stronger than raw safety.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Removing a finite fragment F from a support subtracts the exact rational finite Mersenne sum from the value; that rational has odd reduced denominator whose multiplicative order of 2 is exactly the lcm of F. Combining with the denominator sandwich gives a certificate carrying the exact residual value, the exact period, and the transported wrap-ratio lower bound on the residual's reciprocal mass.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The transport is unconditional; its wrap-ratio output inherits the rationality hypothesis of the T9 layer through hwhole.

If a support containing {2,3} (respectively {2,3,6,7,14}) has value exactly 1/2 and its residual above that fragment is nonempty, then the residual's reciprocal sum diverges or exceeds the wrap ratio attached to the fragment's lcm.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The raw common-denominator coordinates of the greedy prefix differ from the reduced ones by exactly the gcd reduction factor, and every excess inequality in raw coordinates is equivalent to the corresponding inequality in reduced coordinates; membership in the greedy prefix support at rank a is the take test at that rank.

The greedy remainder for 1/2 equals (an integer carry minus the binary incidence tail of the finite prefix support) over 2^(n+1); the support tail gap equals the excess numerator over the prefix denominator; and the bad-skip cap violation is exactly a two-sided window condition on that support-coefficient tail gap.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This is the bridge that puts the greedy lane and the divisor-incidence lane in the same coordinates.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A take step of the reduced greedy state has an exact closed form: the new numerator and denominator are given by explicit polynomials in the old ones, the coprimality is preserved, the residual numerator and the exact cancellation factor are computed, and the actual greedy orbit realises this step, so a raw taken residual reduces to the next displayed state by a positive factor.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Exact arithmetic of the actual greedy orbit; unconditional but with no irrationality consequence on its own.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A nonzero n has exactly 2^omega(n) squarefree divisors, so the divisor incidence of the support of squarefree integers at least two is 2^omega(n) - 1; this is odd at every n >= 2 and never zero there.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The count of squarefree divisors as 2^omega is textbook multiplicative number theory; the parity and positivity corollaries are immediate.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For any coefficient sequence, if the base-b carried aggregate of the first block of length K >= 1 is divisible by b^K, then b divides the coefficient at the last position of that block, because every other term carries a positive power of b.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A one-line base-b digit extraction, but it is the actual engine of the squarefree barrier and applies to every coefficient sequence, not only the squarefree one.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: At the squarefree support and every even base b >= 2, the two block-certificate engines that impose a FIRST-BLOCK DIVISIBILITY condition - the digitwise one and the carry-aware one - have no instance: already at precision q = b^2 no tuple (N, K, L, C) satisfies either schema. Blocks of length K >= 1 die by parity, because the carried first block forces b to divide an odd coefficient, and K <= 1 dies by density, because the incidence is at least 1 from n = 2 on and the middle block alone exhausts the budget b^L. Both steps consume the divisibility hypothesis, so the argument does not extend to the divisibility-free low-carry engine (see scope_caveat).
statement_nodes.engine: parity of 2^omega(n) - 1 plus density of the incidence
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The file itself states the honest scoping; this node preserves it. This is the barrier whose scope was previously overstated.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Does NOT rule out: (1) THE LOW-CARRY RESIDUE-BAND ENGINE. irrational_coeff_series_of_weighted_coeff_low_carry_block_certificates (Erdos249257/CertificateKernel.lean:14707) is a third, strictly weaker arbitrary-coefficient engine, and it is NOT closed here. It imposes no divisibility condition on the first block at all - only the height inequality q * (V * b^(L-K) + C + (N+L+2)) < b^L with V = (sum over r in Icc 1 K of c(N+r) * b^(K-r)) mod b^K - so dvd_last_of_carry_block has nothing to attack, the parity of 2^omega(n) - 1 is irrelevant to it, and the K <= 1 density step never triggers because K is no longer forced down. It reaches the squarefree support by exactly the two steps the other two engines use (erdosSupportSeries_eq_tsum_supportCoeff plus supportCoeff_le_self), so the absence of an erdosSupportSeries-level wrapper is bookkeeping, not scope. This is the same third-engine gap that was nearly published once; do not restate this barrier as closing the block-certificate family. (2) The irrationality of the squarefree-support value itself, which is open and untouched. (3) Odd bases - the hypothesis hbeven : 2 divides b is used essentially. (4) The shifted support obtained by adjoining 1, which has the same irrationality question and does admit full digitwise opening blocks of every length (see adjoining_one_is_value_free_and_repairs_the_parity). (5) Any irrationality engine outside the block-certificate schemas - in particular the lcm-gap engine irrational_erdosSum_of_lcm_gap, the near-integer engine, and the periodic/residue-class specialisations of CertificateKernel are entirely unaffected. (6) Universal Erdos #257, since the argument is about one specific support. The obstruction is a property of the coefficient normalisation 2^omega(n) - 1, not of the support.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Adjoining 1 to the squarefree support adds the rational 1/(b - 1), so irrationality of the squarefree-support value holds IF AND ONLY IF irrationality of the shifted-support value holds; the shifted incidence is 2^omega(n), which is even at every n >= 2, and for every block length K there is a position at which the full digitwise opening condition of the base-2 engine holds. The parity obstruction therefore does not survive the shift. The headline is an iff between two statements NEITHER of which is decided anywhere in the corpus, so it transports an open question rather than settling one; the decided content is the coefficient identity and the Chinese-remainder block existence.
open_antecedents: Both sides of irrational_erdosSupportSeries_squarefreeSupport_iff_shifted are open: Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b squarefreeSupport) is undecided (the module docstring says so explicitly), and Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b squarefreeShiftedSupport) is undecided for the same reason. The iff is proved, but it establishes nothing about either value.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The repair is the load-bearing honesty statement of the module: it converts the barrier from a claim about the support into a claim about a normalisation choice. statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For every K there is a positive N with omega(N + r) >= r for all 1 <= r <= K, by reserving disjoint blocks of r fresh primes for each shift r and applying the Chinese remainder theorem.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A standard CRT construction for prescribed prime-factor counts on consecutive shifts; classical in flavour, and the corpus makes no novelty claim.
